description: This map depicts 30-year normal annual precipitation in inches (in) for the Continental 48 States (1991–2020), based on the Parameter-elevation Regressions on Independent Slopes Model (PRISM) developed by the PRISM Climate Group at Oregon State University.

This map depicts 30-year normal annual maximum temperature in degrees Fahrenheit (°F) for the Continental 48 States (1991–2020), based on the Parameter-elevation Regressions on Independent Slopes Model (PRISM) developed by the PRISM Climate Group at Oregon State University.

This map depicts 30-year normal annual minimum temperature in degrees Fahrenheit (°F) for the Continental 48 States (1991–2020), based on the Parameter-elevation Regressions on Independent Slopes Model (PRISM) developed by the PRISM Climate Group at Oregon State University.
This map depicts the estimated 100-year floodplains for the Continental 48 States for 2016.

This layer is derived from the 2018 version of the gSSURGO 30m (continental 48 States and Washington D.C.) and 10m rasters (all other regions) produced by the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS). The value for drainage class is derived from the gSSURGO map unit aggregated attribute table field Drainage Class - Dominant Condition (drclassdcd). The SSURGO variable natural drainage class (dominant condition) was selected for use in EnviroAtlas because it indicates soil wetness or degree of saturation.

This National Wetlands Inventory (NWI) map, developed by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS), maps and classifies wetlands across the U.S. State and local government agencies use NWI in planning to identify local wetlands and to limit and mitigate wetland losses during economic development.

Land Cover from NLCD (National Land Cover Database) classifications are based primarily on Landsat data along with ancillary data sources, such as topography, census and agricultural statistics, soil characteristics, wetlands, and other land cover maps. NLCD 2025, produced by Multi-Resolution Land Characteristics (MRLC) Consortium, is a 16-class land cover classification scheme that has been applied consistently across the Continental 48 States at a spatial resolution of 30 meters. For additional information, go to https://www.mrlc.gov/. See https://viewer.nationalmap.gov/help for assistance with The National Map viewer, services, or metadata.
